a1
This is the family line of Esau, who is also called Edom, the brother of Jacob.
a2
Esau took three wives, two Canaanite women and Ishmael's daughter Basemath. They bore him sons in Canaan.
b1
His household and herds grew so large that the land could not hold his and Jacob's together.
b2
So Esau took his wives, his children, and all his livestock, and moved to the hill country of Seir, away from his brother Jacob.
c1
There his family grew. The text names his sons and grandsons, and they became chiefs of clans in the land of Edom.
c2
It also lists the people who lived in Seir before him, and their clans.
d1
It lists the kings who ruled in Edom before any king ruled over the people of Israel.
e1
The chapter closes with the clans of Esau, by their families and the places where they lived.
h1
After meeting in peace, Esau and Jacob went separate ways.
h2
The text gives one reason: their herds were too many for one land.
h3
Peace does not always mean living side by side.
h4
Today, pray for someone you had to part from, and wish them well.
i
Who can you bless, even from far away?
